newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian banks support new housing financing plan.
newsitem.headline: Croatian banks support new housing financing plan.

text.p: Croatian bankers gave a green light on Tuesday to draft housing legislation, designed to help impoverished citizens obtain long-term loans at managable rates.

"We welcome the proposals from a pragmatic point of view, because they will provide us, banks with additional business," Neven Dobrovic, president of the association of banks and other financial institutions, told a meeting.
The two draft laws, which will shortly get their second reading in Croatian parliament -- the Sabor -- come ahead of the nationwide regional and municipal elections on April 13.
They were presented to banks by the author Djuro Njavro, a member of parliament from the ruling party (HDZ) ranks and economic adviser to President Franjo Tudjman.
Njavro cited a recent poll in which a majority of Croatians, asked what they would do if they had more money, said they would use it to buy or renovate their houses and flats.
"The idea is to have loans with as long a term as possible at the lowest possible interest," he said.
In the past, some three of four percent of the salaries were used by the state to finance onstruction of flats, let at nominal rents.
Instead, the government now plans to pour some 360 million kuna ($60.5 million) of budget money each year into a new fund to subsidise borrowing by poorer citizens.
The other proposal envisages creating institutions of the building society type which would attract long-term savings of 1,200 German marks or more annually.

Commercial banks are charging around nine percent annual interest but no more than a mere 5-10 percent of the population, earning an average 2,200 kuna per month, can afford to buy their own place to live.
"Our goal is to increase that segment to betwen 20 and 30 percent," Njavro said.
